Dust-storm haze overhead, a thick tan suspended diffusion above the entire brick settlement, the light arriving from no single direction, every surface coated in a low-contrast warm-beige wash, the far false-fronts fading to near-invisibility.

Dust-storm ambient wash, the overhead haze turning all direct light into a diffuse yellow-tan blanket, the brick street and wagon details rendered flat and equal, hard shadows gone, the whole scene wrapped in a murky ochre veil.

Dust-storm low-contrast flood, a tan-filtered overhead source pressing down on the brick mine entrance and ore-cart tracks, the normally crisp stud shadows softened to faint smudges, the atmosphere thickening to a gritty amber soup beyond ten bricks.

Campfire trailside glow, a low trans-orange source at ground-center, the warm flame-light radiating outward across the circle of cowboy figures and saddle-brick details, the surrounding plate-ground fading into deep night-blue within a short radius.

Campfire canyon-floor, the trans-orange flame source nestled between the brick rock formations, its warm orange-red glow catching the underside of every overhang brick and the faces of resting figures, the canyon walls behind in deep blue-black.

Campfire trailhead ring, the low trans-orange source throwing a warm dome of amber light across the brick chuck-wagon side and tin-cup details, the darkness beyond the fire circle an immediate and total deep blue.

Lightning-flash prairie strike, a trans-yellow bolt source from upper-left, the momentary burst bleaching the brick mesa and flat-plate grassland to stark white-yellow, hard multiple shadows thrown in every direction from every figure and post.

Lightning-flash canyon, the trans-yellow overhead burst catching the top face of every brick ledge and rock-stack in sharp cold-white while the undercuts drop to instant black, the whole canyon geology rendered in a single violent exposure.

Lightning-flash mine entrance, the trans-yellow bolt outside the tunnel mouth flooding the brick timber frame and ore-cart in harsh white-yellow from the right, the tunnel interior beyond retreating into absolute darkness by contrast.

Stagecoach lantern rolling dark-trail, the warm trans-orange bulb-source mounted at coach-left, its amber cone lighting the nearest brick road plates and the horse-team haunches, the boardwalk and tree-stumps beyond the beam staying in deep trail-black.

Stagecoach dual lanterns, the paired trans-orange sources flanking the driver's box, their overlapping warm glow washing the front brick wheel rims and road tiles in amber, the prairie darkness pressing in from all sides beyond the coach.

Stagecoach lantern canyon pass, the single trans-orange source swaying at the right corner of the coach, its moving amber beam catching one brick canyon wall in warm patches while the opposite wall remains in cool blue-grey shadow.

Mine interior miner's lamp, the dim trans-amber helmet source aimed forward, its tight warm cone illuminating the nearest brick tunnel wall planks and ore-vein details while the tunnel recedes into heavy charcoal darkness behind the figure.

Mine shaft lamp bracket, a small trans-amber source fixed to the brick support beam, its low warm glow pooling on the plate-floor below and catching the pickaxe prop, the tunnel beyond the bracket fading to near-black instantly.

Mine cart lamp, the trans-amber lantern clipped to the ore-cart front, its faint warm cone lighting the immediately surrounding brick track tiles and rubble details, the low ceiling above staying in shadow and the far shaft invisible.

Railroad train headlamp, the powerful trans-yellow beam source mounted on the locomotive front, the cone of cold-yellow light cutting across the brick prairie-plate track and ballast stones, the night beyond the beam an unbroken blue-black.

Railroad headlamp approach, a strong trans-yellow source from far left tracking toward the brick depot platform, the beam washing the rail-tile surface and signal-post in sharp yellow while the platform shelter stays in warm lantern contrast.

Ghost-town abandoned diffuse, faint moonlight scattered through cloud, a dim silver-blue ambient source with no clear direction, the deserted brick main-street and swinging-door details equally grey-lit and equally quiet, deep shadow in every doorway.

Ghost-town empty street, the diffuse cloud-filtered moonlight spreading a low cool-grey wash across the entire brick settlement, no dominant shadow direction, every surface faded and bleached of color, the broken windows dark and hollow.

Railyard sodium-amber lamp, the overhead warm-orange source casting deep pools of amber on the brick switching platform and rail ties while the spaces between lamp posts fall into heavy brown-black industrial shadow.

Railyard switchyard sodium, the orange-amber lamps spaced along the brick depot wall, each one throwing a soft warm circle on the plate-ground below and leaving the mid-spans between posts in dim orange-grey half-darkness.

Blue-hour prairie ambient, the cool dim post-sunset source wrapping the brick open-range scene in muted blue-grey, only the far mesa rim catching the last sliver of warm amber on its top-course studs, the foreground cold and still.

Blue-hour last light, the cool blue ambient settling on the brick cattle-pen and bunkhouse while a faint warm-orange band on the right horizon edge catches the top of the water-tower in a single thin warm line.

Solar-eclipse shadow, the sudden ambient drop rendering the brick main-street in a strange cool flat twilight at midday, colors desaturated to grey-green, all normal shadows gone, the scene lit by an eerie sourceless ring-light.

Blizzard snow-storm whiteout, the diffuse white overhead source killing all directional contrast, the brick fort walls and cavalry figures equally pale, every surface dusted in grey-white scattered light, the distance a total white void.

Bonfire ranch-BBQ glow, a large trans-orange source at ground-center behind the brick ranch fence, the big warm fire casting flickering orange light across the corral planks and seated-figure details, the open sky above a deep indigo.

High-noon harsh top-light, a direct overhead key throwing short hard shadows straight down off every false-front and hitching post, bleaching the tan-plate main-street to bone-white, the unforgiving frontier sun leaving no escape.

Golden-dusk low silhouette, warm amber raking the length of the brick main-street from the west, buildings and a lone mounted figure thrown into long dark silhouette against the copper-orange horizon plates.

Saloon oil-lamp warm, pools of trans-orange lamp-glow spreading across the brick bar-top and poker-table tiles, the ceiling rafters and far corners sinking into smoky brown-shadow, the cozy-but-tense interior lamp-light.

Moonlit graveyard cool, a high silver-blue moon casting soft overhead light across the cross-topped headstones and the dusty grey-plate ground, deep cool shadows pooling between every brick fence post.

Sunrise pink-amber side-light, a low eastern source raking warm pink-gold across the prairie grass-plate and wooden ranch fencing, long gentle shadows stretching west across the flat tan-brick ground.

Dust-storm haze overhead, a diffuse tan-amber wash suspended from above and all sides, flattening contrast across the mesa-plate cliff-face and street, every brick edge softened under the gritty suspended pall.

Campfire trailside glow, a low central trans-orange flame-source casting upward warm-amber light on the circle of cowboy figures and the brick log-ring, the surrounding prairie plates sinking into deep ink-blue night.

Lightning-flash trans-yellow, a sudden harsh side-strike from the right freezing the mesa rock-plate and prairie in a split-second of cold yellow-white light, every stud and brick edge hard-lit and stark.

Stagecoach lantern warm, a pair of low forward-mounted trans-orange bulb-sources throwing a rolling warm pool down the dark brick trail-plates ahead, the coach sides catching amber edge-glow against the black night.

Mine interior lamp dim, a single miner's trans-amber head-lamp casting a tight low cone forward onto the rough rock-plate tunnel walls, the brick shaft beyond the beam dropping into near-total darkness.
